notes.title: Fallen Graces
notes.content:
[b][h2]Greetings, Misfits![/h2][/b]
We know it’s a bit frustrating to see these dark silhouettes under the available characters. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/oWXrmRl.png[/img]
[i][b]Who are they? What do they do? Why do they do what they do? [/b][/i]

These are the questions we aim to delve into with this devlog to ease the everlasting itch of seeing unavailable content. 

Meet the future outcasts! Their past was full of tales, yet now they have nobody but themselves. And even though the remains of society does not care for them, they struggled enough to acquire skills needed for life in the wasteland. These are the people who could save you or mug you. Maybe even both at the same time.

[h2][i][b]Mercenary[/b][/i] [i](Support + Elimination)[/i][/h2]

Ex-guard at Vapor Wave Inc, carrying heavy armor and a Vapor Wave Inc Gun [i](all rights reserved)[/i], capable of [b]both destroying enemies and giving shields to party members.[/b] Also his corporate background may get you out of certain situations without making use of brute force.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/gBarlYB.png[/img]



[b]His past?[/b] [i]Morally dubious. [/i]
[b]His character?[/b] [i]Complicated. [/i]
[b]His motivation?[/b] [i]That would be a spoiler.[/i]

His biggest strength is scaling his power with almost every buff — be it shield, armor or ability power. And he can also buff himself! And his teammates! Sounds overpowered? Well, no. 

Given a couple of levels, he can carry his team through the fight, but early in the campaign [i](and perhaps further, if you make poor choices)[/i] Mercenary has to depend heavily on his teammates before his potential is fully unlocked. This guy benefits from being your favorite and getting the best upgrades and gear.

[h3][b]Refresh Ability: Vapor Wave Inc. Gun[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExNjJvN3ZzNnozbW81a2d6MnljbHN5NnMxbXVqNmVvNWJhY2RubGxyNyZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/9Ae8oSxV9T2voQkifK/source.gif[/img]
[i]Deal [b]1-2[/b] damage to an enemy line and refresh other abilities.[/i]

The only refresh ability in the game with damage to several targets. [b]Scales with Ability Power.[/b] 
Once given enough buffs, gear and crit luck it can remove a whole line of enemies from the fight in one turn. 

Don’t have Ability Power? No problem, after an upgrade [b]the damage can scale with shields Mercenary has.[/b] This upgrade has a great synergy with his other abilities.

[h3][b]Stand Your Ground[/b][/h3][img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExaWhjazFlYmN3cWw1OWQ2dzNzYjhydmZkZWcweXdobGNrOGN4M2h2eCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/7qBXIa8DTjWT0iZynv/source.gif[/img]
[i]Give shields to yourself and your ally. [b]Scales with AP.[/b][/i]

Should we even explain why an ability that gives shields to two party members at once without drawbacks and scaling with AP is an extremely good ability? With an alternative upgrade Mercenary can give more shields to himself — at the cost of not protecting his allies, [i]you wouldn’t selfishly leave this cute baby lizard without shields, would you?[/i]

[h3][b]Shield to the Head[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExcjN3OGpveTYzMG1sY2htaDhjOHEyYjVhMHY0cTZ5OTdvaHVsdGZjcSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/ZXTtcyaYJc7rwSznln/source.gif[/img]
[i]Deal [b](3 + amount of your shields)[/b] damage and null your shields[/i]

[i]This is an optional ability that suits Mercenary best. It’s your good old [b]«All-In» ability[/b]. «Shield to the Head»[/i] can easily disintegrate a completely healthy and strong enemy in one action if Mercenary has enough shields. 

Its potential is easily unlocked if one of your support characters has [i][b]«Safe Haven»[/b][/i], that gives an insane amount of shields if nobody plans to attack the target.[i] Additionally,[/i] give Mercenary a [i]Shield Generator[/i] (gives 5 shields at the start of the battle). And [i]«Shield to the Head»[/i] can already deal enough damage to [i]turn a formidable foe into Vapor™![/i] 

[i]And it’s just the beginning.[/i]

[i][b]With correct execution Mercenary can even do THIS![/b][/i]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExa3NvYTMzdDRxYWFqazBxNmFlbmwwdWpxcmY1MjVwajNmb2t3YjFrYiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/GxFmtk6aenUbjycGQX/source.gif[/img]
[i](It didn’t help, he died afterwards anyway, BUT THIS IS NOT THE POINT)[/i]

[b]Alright, who else we got?[/b]

[h2][b]Rogue[/b] [i](Elimination + Maneuver)[/i][/h2]

A former gang member, who [b]did not[/b] leave on good terms. You bet she holds a grudge. And a knife. Two, actually.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/r208Ptm.png[/img]


She doesn’t have much HP. To be frank, it’s actually the lowest HP of all playable characters. [b]However![/b] Your HP doesn’t matter if you don’t get hit! And this is the basis for her fighting style. [i][b]She doesn’t block the hit, she evades it.[/b][/i] 

And may [i](insert a name of a deity here)[/i] help the poor fools, who decide not to attack her at all. [b]Her main strength is striking when the opponents aren’t looking.[/b]

When there is no fight, she exceeds at gambling (by cheating), can guide you through any kind of dirty slums, and occasionally saves you from being mugged by her fellow highwaymen.

[h3][b]Refresh Ability: Sneak Attack[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExeDRqN2hseWhhenFrODEyM3Jpd3IzNDh6d3c0eXY3eTM5YWNhZTh5MiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/vdSxsk1vjMDShZMh54/source.gif[/img]
[b]Deal 1 damage to an enemy. Deal 4 if nobody plans to attack Rogue.[/b] [i]Scales with Ability Power.[/i]

As it can be used every turn, it is her main source of damage. With an upgrade it can also apply vulnerability to enemies. If she fails to oneshot the enemy, her teammate won’t. 

[i]Do you know why there is always Savage in the background? [/i]
[b]Because he can always provoke enemies, so Rogue can use her attacks effectively. [/b]

[i]And do you know why there are so many critical strikes? [/i]
[b]Because «Sneak Attack» has 25% crit chance by default.[/b] If it still isn’t enough - give her the «Daredevil» personality, that allows her to land critical strikes even more often. 

If your damage expectations are insatiable, you can also equip her with [i]«Neverender»[/i], with which she will get a bonus action every time she crits. [b]Yes, you can attack 2, 3, 4 times in one turn as long as all of the attacks are critical successes.[/b]

[i]“But what if it still doesn’t crit?”[/i]
[b]Fret not, there’s always a way to deal damage reliably![/b] For example, let’s take a look at one of the level-up abilities:

[h3][b]Foolproof Plan[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExZXV1YjFkeWZrdnJoZm14dGlzYzVjdDNqZjcxa2pwbnJxZXMycG5naSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/0bEsZiC2MiMFmTG95X/source.gif[/img]
Make your next action a [b]critical success, gain +1 Ability Power for it[/b]

Although it may look like mere verbal aggression, it is one of the best tools in the game for [i]playing safe[/i]. With a proper setup [i]«Sneak Attack»[/i]  after this ability can deal 10 or more damage. [i]Should we remind you, that most attacks rarely deal more than 4?[/i]

[b]Moving on to your defences![/b]

[h3][b]Avoid Contact[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExNTVndWJ6OHl6cHA5b2syZGJhYmZ2ZGU3d3d1MDExaGI5amhhcndobCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/PmXElZKtC8LKLelOEh/source.gif[/img]
[b]Evade[/b] the next enemy attack. Gain +1 Ability Power for your next action.

[b]This one is Rogue’s bread and butter.[/b] This greatly compensates for her lack of HP and sometimes can be more effective than letting your tank, well, [i]tank[/i] the damage. It doesn’t matter whether the attack has 2 damage or 20 if it misses. With one of the upgrades the ability also buffs her if she has full HP. 

Playing with Rogue in your team is tricky, but this is what makes it so fun. [b]Her basic skill set makes her self-sufficient[/b], but it’s for you to decide as she levels up if she gets more skills to help her allies — or to hurt her enemies.

[b]Speaking of helping allies, here’s a support character![/b]

[h2][b]Alchemist[/b] [i](Support + Maneuver)[/i][/h2]

A [i]former[/i] member of the Technomancer Guild who has outstayed his welcome in the community for very clear reasons. He also smells funny. Must be his concoctions.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/DB5npYL.png[/img]



He is [i]weird[/i]. But he is neither aware of it nor ashamed of it. As a support character, his abilities consist of buffs and debuffs. He provides great defense for his allies and is capable of applying almost every negative effect in the game. Furthermore, he makes use of all the chemicals you find on your journey! Suspicious mushrooms, barrels of toxic sludge, or any other hazardous substance, it all goes in the soup if you let him do the cooking.

[b]But he’s an alchemist, not a chemist[/b], testing solutions isn’t his thing, that’s why their advantages always come with drawbacks. If you want your Alchemist to be effective, better build the whole party around him. [i]He isn’t your сonventional «buff-you-debuff-them» type of support.[/i]

[h3][b]Refresh Ability: Alkaliquor v0.4[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMjc3dW13NjhvMHdocjcwbXhieHY3ZGR6anRicTRocDBlbHUydXBkcSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/oUlF5SfGTw1FVAo9io/source.gif[/img]
Give enemy [b][i]«Life-Loss 2»[/i][/b] and [b]+1 armor[/b] for the whole battle

[i]«Life-Loss»[/i] deals a little damage to HP every turn, ignoring shields and armor. 
But armor reduces incoming attack damage from all attacks. It implies that this ability isn’t the best for quick elimination by collective effort of the whole team, but rather sets up a long fight to wear enemies out. 

This combines greatly with Tamer’s skills, one of which can trigger [i]«Life-Loss»[/i] one more time and another provides retaliation to enemy attacks, thus allowing you to go for a passive playstyle, focusing on defence and letting enemies die by themselves.

Alternatively, its upgraded variant, instead of giving armor, gives the enemy attack damage bonus, so you can kill him quicker, but he will be able to do the same. Understandably, buffing enemies sometimes can make matters worse, but you may have to use this ability to refresh other ones. If you are lucky enough, you can equip Alchemist with [i]«Stun Baton»[/i], an item that allows refreshing abilities with basic attack.

Obviously, if enemies die slowly, they have more chances to make [i]you[/i] die. This is when Alchemist’s defensive abilities come into play. 

[h3][b]Preventive Painkiller[/b][/h3]
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExbmg2MjdudnNzN2xheTlzaGx0OGI5NzE5ZWlpMHBmejhheXh1MWN2MCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/NumEDkiZANbZIPLX3w/source.gif[/img]
Give an ally (or yourself) [b]+3-4 armor[/b] until the end of turn.

We could’ve just written, «make an ally almost invincible». [i]«Preventive Painkiller»[/i] makes any ally, even the baby lizard, withstand heavy and painful attacks without losing too much HP. The more hits the target takes, the more damage is negated. This is why it’s twice as effective if the ally can provoke enemies.

As you can see, there is plenty of room to experiment, combining characters with different personalities, upgrading abilities, or straight up replacing them, enhancing their performance with items and unique traits, unlocking secret abilities with new mechanics… 

Honestly, there is too much to fit in one devlog: secret abilities, unique encounters and interactions, countless combinations of personality traits and character relationships. There is no way to describe it thoroughly, only to experience it yourself.

We can go on but [i]it’s time to stop.[b] For now.[/b][/i]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2551970/Outcast_Tales/

We hope this devlog has given you a better understanding of what’s to come when the game goes gold! [b]Before that we will be releasing an update to The First Journey[/b][i], so you can mentally prepare for the dangers that await you.[/i]

If you are as eager to see Outcast Tales in full bloom as we are, feel free to follow our Twitter page and wishlist the game on Steam to be the first to know about all news related to the game. In the meantime, if you haven't already, you should really consider playing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/882590/Outcast_Tales_The_First_Journey/]the First Journey prologue[/url]! 

Now that you know more about the characters, [i]who is your favourite? How do you think they might interact with eachother? Who would be the best (or worst) baby lizard parent?[/i] Share your thoughts with CRITICAL REFLEX Discord community! 

[h3][b]See you soon![/b][/h3]
[url=https://discord.gg/Rf7MyFhwU4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44836977/3cc1cc61976ca719139d69ac8a06f14712f9954d.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: The Other Tales
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, Misfits![/h3]

The release of [i]Outcast Tales[/i] is getting closer. We hope the game provides plenty of fun for everyone, with many hours of content to take a crack at. But don’t just sit on your hands simply replaying [i]The First Journey[/i] over and over in anticipation, as [b]we will be releasing an update to The First Journey[/b], so you might want to wait before jumping into adventure with fresh eyes. 
How about you play or watch something else for now instead? And that’s why we’re here today.

Together, we are going to take a look at media with obvious similarities to Outcast Tales; some of it might’ve even inspired us in some ways! Hopefully, these stories will tide you over while you’re biting your nails off in wait for the game.

[h3]Death Road to Canada (2016)[/h3]

It’s a zombie apocalypse and only your dim-witted friends can save you! Explore the cute and quirky side of post-civilizational mayhem, ward off zombies with a bunch of random items, and survive while ransacking locations for fuel and resources.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/fSNaYxB.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/fLyucEx.png[/img]
The idea of a team of unique characters going on a large, semi-randomized adventure definitely was a big inspiration for the general progression of Outcast Tales. We really wanted our game to have tons of items, unique events, and character interactions that make every playthrough feel different. And yet, even with all the carnage going on, each new run still manages to tell a unique story and create a fun memory.

The big highlight for us were the car rides in-between the action locations: each one sets up some sort of a unique scenario and mini-story, lets the player do a meaningful choice that changes the outcome of their playthrough or affects their resources, and also acts as a springboard for character dialogue and fun banter. Having these episodes accomplish multiple goals at the same time while keeping things brisk and breezy is something we definitely learned from for our Campfire sections.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/doCNxoc.gif[/img]
[h3]Trigun (1998)[/h3]

Surely you expected a Western picture to be a big inspiration, didn’t you? Many probably expected something closer to [i]The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly[/i], though…

Both [i]Trigun[/i] and Outcast Tales fall into the category of “Western”, but only metaphorically so: things don’t [i]literall[/i]y take place in the Wild West (in fact, both take place in the far future), but things do happen against a somewhat desert-y backdrop meant to symbolize an unconquered frontier.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/iVUu0EU.jpeg[/img]

What really sets these apart is injecting a hearty dose of comedy into the usually stoic setting, with both Vash and your main party bouncing off other characters in unexpected ways (that said, Outcast Tales definitely brings [i]even more[/i] havoc to the table).

It isn’t all smiles and laughs, though: as you watch or read Trigun, deeper layers will come into play, revealing secret pasts and clandestine conspiracies. While this isn’t exactly the template used in Outcast Tales, we [i]did[/i] want to highlight a few more thought-provoking moments throughout the adventure: as you play, your party will be faced with plenty of funny and somber choices, leading to unexpected and permanent consequences. A lot of these moments are played for laughs, but they’re often based on some type of a real moral dilemma, and we hope these sequences give you a nice opportunity to engage with the game on a slightly deeper level.
Sometimes just stopping and thinking for a few moments makes the ensuing carnage all that sweeter, you know? It’s just a few moments, though!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/tZnsz8q.png[/img]
[h3]Slay the Spire (2019)[/h3]

You might have expected that, and it’s no surprise, as the games do share some of the DNA.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/47QUhFv.jpeg[/img]
Obviously, Outcast Tales is not a deck builder game, but what we really wanted to hone into are the tactics surrounding your opponents. Each battle in [i]Slay the Spire[/i] is an event that requires you to plan your deck accordingly and engage in an arduous fight that will test your planning, wits, and maybe a little bit of your luck.

For Outcast Tales, we aimed to take that feeling of each fight being an important, boss-like event, and boosting the strategic factor way up.

You are not dealt a deck of cards this time, but you are also not braving the sandstorms all alone. The key factor to every battle is your party composition and being able to plan around your team’s moves and long-term growth. 
Most importantly, Outcast Tales lets you view the upcoming turns and actions of your opponents. All the machinations are laid bare, which lets you focus on the strategizing aspect of a particular fight. Your luck really only matters for the critical hits and out-of-battle scenarios.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/9P4fmTx.png[/img]
We hope the tactical nature of our game’s battle system produces plenty of synergies with your customizable party and the myriad of random events, making each run truly a unique experience and a tale to be told and retold.

[h3]The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy (1978-1979)[/h3]

Last but not least. Let’s address what is possibly the biggest highlight of Outcast Tales: the writing.
We always wanted to zero in on the concept of making an RPG rougelite game. But is it really a true RPG if you don't have miles upon miles of optional dialogue that dives deep into every characters’ personal history, the worldbuilding, and the social mores that echo our own predicaments?
We thought so too, so instead we filled the game to the brim with jokes and outrageous situations to make it as shareable and repostable as possible.

In all seriousness, [i]The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy[/i] is a brilliant piece of writing and a masterpiece of sci-fi satire, and if you haven’t listened to it, or read it, or at least watched it — you really should.
What makes it special for us, is that it deconstructs its genre while still preserving what makes it fun for the readers in the first place. Taking the sci-fi tropes and plot contrivances and cranking them up to eleven doesn’t take away from the core aspects of a sci-fi story, nor does it make the [i]what-if[/i] philosophical quandaries less compelling; lampshading the trappings of the genre only ends up making them shine brighter. That, and we just wouldn’t be able to live without the thick, succulent paste of its British cheekiness.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/wqv8b0n.png[/img][i]A moment from the 2005 movie adaptation[/i]

For Outcast Tales, we strived to do a similar thing for the Western genre, post-apocalyptic scenarios, and sci-fi, all rolled into one. We even brought in [b]Samuel Barnett[/b] to do [i]the voice[/i] and provide the game with that missing Englishman touch.
Of course, we wouldn’t be able to preserve [i]exactly[/i] the same narrative structure due to the game’s interactive and randomized nature. However, we’re hoping the writing chops will shine through in a myriad of character encounters, scenarios that skirt the line between hilarious and morbid, and all the billions of words of character dialogue we’re working on.
Outcast Tales can be many things, but at the end of the day we hope it becomes a fun [i]and[/i] funny story for you to experience and share with others.

[h3]***[/h3]

So how was that for a trip down the memory lane? Obviously, these weren’t the only influences on Outcast Tales — we’ve also been inspired by even more video games, Terry Prachett, and our tabletop sessions, among a multitude of other media.

We hope sharing those with you gave you some insight into our creative process. Who knows, maybe you’ll even pick up some new favorites and have something to scratch that itch before the inevitable release of the game!

But enough about us: what is it that makes [i]you[/i] excited for Outcast Tales? Are there certain inspirations you’re looking forward to? A certain gameplay mechanic you like, or a feeling you wish to capture?
Share all of it on the CRITICAL REFLEX Discord server! And don’t forget to follow our Twitter page and wishlist the game on Steam to stay posted on all the upcoming updates.

See you soon!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2551970/Outcast_Tales/

notes.title: A Day's Journey — Part 1
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, misfits![/h3]

...Who am I talking to? You three, obviously. You’ve got an important mission today, so let’s get on with it. Time for another day in the Wasteland. Let’s see if it proves fruitful, shall we?

[h2]Setting out[/h2]

Nobody in their right mind would set out for adventure without assembling a party first. The world of Outcast Tales might seem brimming with total loons, and yet you don’t see any of them traveling alone, do you?

Your team member’s personality type will determine their base stats, as well as perks and disadvantages they might receive during dialogue and other specific situations.
Do take a look at the attacks available to your character: one of them is a special and somehow it recharges other moves upon use. Do some attacks give respite to our heroes, somehow? Perhaps it’s just like when you take a break from your office job by moonlighting as a nighttime security guard… or something.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/b4BbOVf.png[/img][i]You can also set up custom names for your heroes, which is a great way to make some of your friends real mad![/i]

Make sure you screen every party member before you set out. So what if all of half of them are good-for-nothing outlaws? You really don’t want a person with a record in your crew in this day and age, trust me.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/V5sietd.png[/img][i]An eye-catcher, a brave if unhinged daredevil, and a hermit pacifist walk into a bar...[/i]

As you examine the map, you realize you can choose your next destination after most encounters. Maps truly are the greatest invention of man. And yet, the first choice is made for you, so you venture forth.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/5hhC2UI.png[/img][i]You can also use this screen to set up camp and heal your party with rations[/i]

[h2]Day 1[/h2]

Alas, you are quickly thrust into battle. But don’t worry just yet: all the moves the enemy is planning are displayed in the upper part of the battle screen. That’s right: you can see the enemy’s turn order, who they’re planning to strike and the type of attack they will use. Let’s see how you fare with this information in mind.
Many of your attacks are also tailored to these strategies.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/9P4fmTx.png[/img]
You use your foreknowledge of the enemy’s next move and execute an attack that deals extra damage to any enemy focused on that character. After you exchange regular blows and set up a protection barrier, you use your foreknowledge to quickly deal with the foes planning to gang up on your pet.
In the end, you emerge victorious, but one of your teammates receives some battle scars, while another receives enough experience for a new perk. Makes you wonder whose experience proved to be more valuable in the end…

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jFh5HcZ.png[/img][i]Choose carefully![/i]
Enough action for one day, eh? However, your encounter is far from over…

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ipiBxmY.gif[/img]
You combine your personal skills with a pinch of luck and trip up the fleeing enemy. As your sarcastic back-and-forth escalates, the outlaw… gives you a vial of his own blood as a parting gift? Wait, what?
Apparently, vast riches await you in his village if you bring this token to the outlaw’s kin. Wouldn’t the villagers beat you up if you come bearing blood of one of their own? Wait, that’s the plan, isn’t it? Nah, couldn’t be it.
A new destination is suddenly marked on your map, so you decide to make your way there.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/EWS6ueA.png[/img]
However, you first make your way to a nearby settlement…

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TRRHLXv.png[/img]
…Which apparently is hosting a tournament. Feeling exhausted, yet hungry for a distraction, you decide not to take part, but still watch the event. This boosts your morale, making you not only a better warrior, but a better comrade to your teammates, which will prove useful really soon.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PgaSdRm.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/0eu9A6N.png[/img]
Short on money, you buy some rations and continue your journey. The next destination might prove dangerous, so you decide to set up camp for the night.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/qojMmZS.gif[/img][i]Apparently our unhinged daredevil has a softer side?..[/i]

And what sort of campfire would it be without a heart-to-heart? Grown adults still do that, right? Apparently, the charming big guy really wants you to add something to your wishlist. You wouldn’t say no to a guy named “Big Buddy”, would you?

We've got to stop there, but this was only half of that crew's adventure. What will await them on Day 2? Fast friends, deadly enemies, or new philosophical quandries? Tune in for the second part of this entry in just a bit!

And while you wait, join our Discord and Twitter and gather round your own campfire with fellow adventurers! See you soon!

notes.title: Outcast Tales: The First Journey is out NOW!
notes.content:
Time to finally set your foot into the dangerous world of Outcast Tales: the game’s free prologue chapter titled Outcast Tales: The First Journey [b]is out now[/b]!

[previewyoutube=T2JRPrdKnPA;full][/previewyoutube]

This release is [b]more than just a demo[/b], but rather an epic introduction to the game proper! The prologue lets you:

[list]
[*] Play the [b]shortened version of the game’s campaign[/b], featuring tons of enemies, items, and unique events
[*] Mix-and-match your run with [b]four heroes[/b] and [b]five personalities[/b] available
[*] Extend your playtime even further by [b]completing Contracts[/b] and [b]earning achievements[/b]
[*] Enjoy the crisp visuals and sound thanks to the [b]revamped art and UI[/b] as well as smooth voicework by Samuel Barnett ([i]Dirk Gently’s Holistic Detective Agency[/i], [i]Cyberpunk 2077[/i])
[*] Boast about your exploits thanks to [b]Twitch integration support[/b]
[*] …and more!
[/list]

We hope this gives you a proper taste of the game to come. Speaking of…

[h2]The full version of Outcast Tales will be released this year![/h2]

Now is the time to set forth, play the prologue, and prepare for journeys to come. Once you do, don’t forget to hop on to our Discord and Twitter and share your exploits with other adventurers!

See you out in the Wasteland!
